title.en: The office boy and Kothamangalam Subbu

heading.en: A frustrated poet and a loyal number two

hook.en: Some people come to a film studio dreaming of fame and end up painting the faces of crowds. Others rise to the very top. What makes the difference?

objectives.en: Describe the office boy and his frustration
Describe Kothamangalam Subbu and his talents
Explain why the office boy resented Subbu

narration.en: Some people come to a film studio dreaming of fame and end up painting the faces of crowds. Others rise to the very top. What makes the difference?

body.en: The office boy in the make-up department was not a boy at all but a man in middle age. He had joined the studio years earlier hoping to become a star, a director, a screenwriter or a lyricist, and he was a bit of a poet. Instead he spent his days applying make-up to crowd players. Frustrated, he blamed Subbu for his failure and complained to the author.

points.en: A middle-aged man called a boy
Dreams of being an actor, writer or lyricist
Paints the faces of crowd players
Blames Subbu for his own frustration

say.en: The office boy is a middle-aged man called a boy. Subbu is the number two at Gemini.
The office boy's dreams went unfulfilled, while Subbu's many talents were used.
One paints crowd players; the other helps shape whole films.
The office boy is bitter, while Subbu is loyal and generous.

prompt.en: Sort each description into The office boy or Kothamangalam Subbu.

text.en: A middle-aged man, not a boy
Hoped to become a star or a director
Blames someone else for his failure
Suggests many ways to shoot a scene
Generous, with a house full of guests

explanation.en: The contrast shows ambition and frustration on one side, and talent and loyalty on the other.

body.en: Subbu was the number two at Gemini Studios and was devoted to the Boss. He could solve any problem in film-making, suggest many ways to shoot a scene, write poems and stories, and act well in supporting roles. He was generous and hospitable, and his house was always full of people. The author suggests that because Subbu was so close to the Boss, he attracted the envy of those who had not succeeded.

points.en: Number two at Gemini; loyal to the Boss
Envied because he was close to the Boss

narration.en: Subbu was the number two at Gemini Studios and was devoted to the Boss. He could solve any problem in film-making, suggest many ways to shoot a scene, write poems and stories, and act well in supporting roles. He was generous and hospitable, and his house was always full of people.

problem.en: Describe Kothamangalam Subbu as the author presents him.

steps.en: Position: number two at Gemini, closely attached to the Boss.
Talents: practical ideas for scenes, poetry, stories, acting.
Nature: generous and hospitable; a house full of people.
Others' view: envied by those like the office boy.

answer.en: Subbu was the talented, loyal and generous number two at Gemini Studios. His creativity in film-making, writing and acting made him valuable to the Boss, though it also made him a target of envy.
